tools.name: nexus_copilot_command

tools.description: List all memory records in the Nexus database

tools.description: Build a context package centered on a specific entity with configurable traversal depth

tools.description: Enhanced context search with intent detection, keywords, and temporal reasoning

tools.description: Analyze text to extract keywords, entities, and temporal references

tools.description: List all graph entities, optionally filtered by type

tools.name: nexus_search_semantic

tools.description: Store semantic fingerprint for a memory

tools.description: Get all entity links for a memory

tools.description: Get all memory links for an entity
tools.name: nexus_get_entity_memory_links

tools.description: Add native file(s)/folder(s) to a project workspace. Scans directories recursively and registers all files.

paths.description: Native paths to add (files or folders)

tools.name: nexus_add_to_workspace

tools.description: Get the workspace file tree for a project
tools.name: nexus_get_workspace

tools.description: Sync workspace: rescan root dirs, remove stale entries, add new files from disk
tools.name: nexus_sync_workspace

tools.description: Index a file into the knowledge graph: reads content, extracts entities (classes, functions, headings, etc.), creates Document entity + sub-entities with relationships. Supports: py, js, ts, rs, go, java, c, cpp, md, json, yaml, toml, html, css, images.

project_id.description: Optional: Project entity UUID to link file to

tools.name: nexus_index_file

tools.description: Index all interpretable files in a folder recursively into the knowledge graph. Skips hidden dirs, target/, node_modules/, __pycache__/.

project_id.description: Optional: Project entity UUID to link files to

tools.name: nexus_index_folder

tools.description: Read and interpret file content: returns summary, extracted entities, and raw text. Does NOT create entities in the graph — use nexus_index_file for that.
tools.name: nexus_read_file_content

tools.description: Create a new file on disk with content. Creates parent directories automatically. Fails if file already exists — use nexus_write_file to overwrite.
tools.name: nexus_create_file

tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Creates parent directories automatically.
tools.name: nexus_write_file

tools.description: Create a directory (and all parent directories) on disk.
tools.name: nexus_create_folder

tools.description: Delete a file or directory (recursive for directories). Use with caution.
tools.name: nexus_delete_file

tools.description: Move or rename a file/directory. Provide either new_path (full destination) or dest_dir + new_name.
tools.name: nexus_move_file

tools.description: Read raw file content as text. Returns the file content without interpretation or entity extraction. Use for reading code, config files, etc.
tools.name: nexus_read_file

tools.description: Create a file in a project workspace — creates on disk AND registers in the workspace database. Use this when an AI wants to save generated code into a Nexus project.

parent_path.description: Absolute path of parent directory in workspace

tools.name: nexus_create_workspace_file

tools.description: Get cumulative token and cost savings statistics: total tokens saved, cost saved (USD), per-day/week/month/year breakdown, average per interaction, and recent interactions. Real data from the database — no estimates.
tools.name: nexus_savings_stats

tools.description: Get a full savings report: aggregate stats PLUS per-model cost breakdown for all 21 supported LLMs (how much the saved tokens would have cost with each model's input price). Use this to answer 'how much money did Nexus save me?'
tools.name: nexus_savings_report

tools.description: Calculate savings for a specific LLM model: how much the saved tokens would have cost with that model's input price. Model names are case-insensitive, e.g. 'GPT-5.6 Terra', 'deepseek v4 flash', 'Claude Opus 5'.

model.description: Model display name (e.g. 'GPT-5.6 Terra', 'DeepSeek V4 Flash')

tools.name: nexus_savings_per_model

tools.description: List all projects (entities with type Project) in the knowledge graph. Use this to enumerate projects and get their IDs for workspace/project-scoped operations.
tools.name: nexus_projects

tools.description: Get all entities linked to a project via relationships, plus the relationships themselves. Use this to see what a project contains (documents, people, decisions, etc.).
tools.name: nexus_project_entities

tools.description: Get all memory records linked to a specific project. Use this to list the memories saved in a project's space.
tools.name: nexus_project_memories

tools.description: Link an entity to a project by creating a relationship (default type: Uses). Use this to attach documents, people, decisions and other entities to a project.

entity_id.description: Entity UUID to link to the project

tools.name: nexus_link_project_entity

tools.description: Rename a workspace entry (file or folder) — renames on disk AND updates the workspace database, including all children. Returns the new absolute path.

new_name.description: New name (file/folder name only, not a full path)

old_path.description: Current absolute path of the entry

tools.name: nexus_workspace_rename

tools.description: Move a workspace entry (file or folder) to another directory — moves on disk (with cross-filesystem fallback) AND updates the workspace database. Returns the new absolute path.

dest_dir.description: Absolute path of the destination directory

source_path.description: Absolute path of the entry to move

tools.name: nexus_workspace_move

tools.description: Delete a workspace entry (file or folder) — deletes from disk AND removes it from the workspace database (including all descendants). Irreversible.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the entry to delete

tools.name: nexus_workspace_delete

tools.description: Remove an entry from the workspace database ONLY — does NOT delete the file/folder from disk. Use this to un-register a file from a project without touching the filesystem.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the entry to remove from the workspace DB

tools.name: nexus_workspace_remove

tools.description: Check all projects for stale folders — returns the list of project_ids whose ALL workspace root directories no longer exist on disk. Use this to detect dead projects before cleanup.
tools.name: nexus_workspace_check_stale

tools.description: Rename a file or folder on disk (not tied to a workspace project). Returns the new absolute path.

new_name.description: New name (file/folder name only, not a full path)

tools.name: nexus_rename_file

tools.description: Recursively delete a folder on disk (not tied to a workspace project). Irreversible.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the folder to delete

tools.name: nexus_delete_folder

tools.description: Scan a folder on disk and return its file tree (FileEntry with children). Use this to inspect a directory before indexing or linking it to a project.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the folder to scan

tools.name: nexus_scan_folder

tools.description: Get the metadata map of an entity (key/value pairs stored on the entity). Returns an empty object if the entity has no metadata.
tools.name: nexus_entity_metadata

tools.description: Record a measured token-savings event manually (baseline vs context usage). Use this to log a savings measurement that the UI would normally record automatically.

irrelevant_fragments.description: Fragments dropped as below the relevance floor

manual_context.description: 1 if the user added context manually this round

used_fragments.description: Fragments actually used in the final answer

tools.name: nexus_savings_record

tools.description: List all available LLM models (via the opencode CLI). Pass free_only=true to list only free models. Use this to discover which models can be selected for AI features.
tools.name: nexus_ai_models

tools.description: Get database statistics: memory count, entity count, relationship count, commit count, snapshot count, and DB file size. Use this for health/status reports.
tools.name: nexus_db_stats

tools.description: Get configuration values. Pass a key to read a single value, or omit key to list ALL configuration entries. Use this to inspect app settings.

key.description: Config key (optional — omit to list all)

tools.name: nexus_config_get

tools.description: Set a configuration value (creates or updates the key). Use this to change app settings programmatically.
tools.name: nexus_config_set

tools.description: Set the trust state of a memory explicitly: Current, Inferred, Superseded, or Conflicted. Use this to mark a memory as outdated, disputed, or re-verified.

state.description: New state: Current | Inferred | Superseded | Conflicted

tools.name: nexus_memory_set_state

tools.description: Mark a memory as explicitly confirmed by a human. The memory state becomes UserConfirmed with a timestamp. Use this to lock in a verified fact.
tools.name: nexus_memory_confirm

tools.description: Record user feedback on a memory: useful, irrelevant, or wrong. One vote per memory — voting the same kind again removes the vote, a different kind switches it. Optionally explain why in 'note'; the explanation is kept and used by the copilot to understand what is right or wrong about the memory. A 'wrong' verdict also marks the memory Conflicted so it stops being trusted as-is.

note.description: Optional explanation of why this feedback was given

tools.name: nexus_memory_feedback

tools.description: Replace an outdated memory with a newer one. The old memory is marked Superseded (never deleted), and a new Current record is created with the new title/content.

old_id.description: UUID of the memory to replace

tools.name: nexus_memory_supersede

tools.description: Get the memory trust lifecycle overview: how many memories are Current, UserConfirmed, Inferred, Superseded, and Conflicted. Use this for a memory-health dashboard.
tools.name: nexus_lifecycle_overview

tools.description: Scan the knowledge graph for duplicate entities (exact + normalized + fuzzy name match). Returns groups of 2+ entities that look like the same thing, with a bestId merge target per group. Use this before merging to review what would be combined.

min_score.description: Minimum Dice similarity (default 0.78). Lower finds more (noisier) groups, higher finds only strong matches.

tools.name: nexus_find_duplicates

tools.description: Merge duplicate entities into one canonical node. The primary is kept; every id in duplicates is merged into it (metadata combined, relationships redirected, duplicates marked Merged). Idempotent.

duplicates.description: UUIDs of the entities to merge into primary

primary.description: UUID of the entity to keep (use bestId from nexus_find_duplicates)

tools.name: nexus_merge_entities

tools.description: Get product metrics that prove Nexus' value: share of queries without manual context, average context precision, used/irrelevant fragments, token savings vs baseline, average build latency, stale memories, memory fixes, and cross-session memory reuse. Use this to answer 'does Nexus actually help?' with measured data.
tools.name: nexus_product_metrics

tools.description: Import all .md/.markdown/.txt files from a folder into the project knowledge base (RAG corpus). Idempotent: unchanged files are skipped, changed files are re-indexed, files removed from disk are pruned. Use this to make a project's documentation searchable by the AI.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the folder to import

tools.name: nexus_docs_import

tools.description: List imported project documents (RAG corpus), newest first. Use this to see what documentation is already indexed before searching.
tools.name: nexus_docs_list

tools.description: Search the imported project documentation (RAG corpus) by a query. Combines keyword overlap with semantic similarity (ONNX embeddings when available). Returns matching documents with relevance scores so the AI can answer questions about the project's own docs.
tools.name: nexus_docs_search

tools.description: Read the project's AGENTS.md instruction file (or another agents file by name). The content is already injected into context packages automatically, but use this to see the exact rules the AI is expected to follow.
tools.name: nexus_agents_read

tools.description: Generate an AGENTS.md from live Nexus data (modules, commands, knowledge base state) and store it as the active instruction file. The 'documentation skill': use this to create or refresh project instructions without writing them by hand.
tools.name: nexus_agents_generate

tools.description: List all registered skills (runnable commands like JS scripts) with their descriptions. Skills are the lightweight alternative to MCP tools — an agent reads the list, picks the relevant one, and runs only it instead of carrying every tool in context.
tools.name: nexus_skills_list

tools.description: Run a registered skill by name with optional arguments. Captures stdout/stderr with a 30-second timeout. Use this to execute a project script or automation without loading the full MCP tool surface.
tools.name: nexus_skills_run

tools.description: Index a folder of source files into the code graph. Symbols (classes, functions, structs, traits) are extracted with the built-in language parsers, and dependency edges (import / require / use / #include / mod) are recorded. Use this to let the AI answer structural questions about a codebase: what depends on what, where a symbol is defined.

folder_path.description: Absolute path of the folder to index

tools.name: nexus_code_import

tools.description: List indexed source files in the code graph, newest first. Use this to see what code has been indexed before searching symbols.
tools.name: nexus_code_list

tools.description: Search symbols (classes, functions, structs, traits, interfaces) by name across all indexed source files. Returns the defining file and language. Use this to locate where something is defined in the project.
tools.name: nexus_code_search

tools.description: Return the dependencies of one indexed source file (by path): what it imports, requires, includes or uses, with internal/external classification. Use this to understand a file's connections in the code graph.
tools.name: nexus_code_deps

tools.description: Return the files in the code graph that depend on the given target (reverse edges, internal only). Use this to answer 'what would be affected by changing X?'
tools.name: nexus_code_dependents

tools.description: Proactive memory radar: scans the whole memory pool and returns what needs attention right now — unresolved conflicts, memories expiring soon, inferred memories never confirmed by a human, and important memories created or changed since the last radar scan. Use this at the start of a session (or when opening a project) to see what the user should review, instead of waiting for a query. Optionally pass markSeen=true to advance the radar checkpoint to now so the next scan only reports what changed afterwards.

markSeen.description: Advance the scan checkpoint to now after building the snapshot (default false)

tools.name: nexus_radar_snapshot

tools.description: Memory rehearsal plan: which memories are due for review right now, ordered by importance. Rehearsal is the spaced-repetition cycle that keeps important knowledge fresh and lets forgotten memories fade. Use this periodically (e.g. at session start) to see what should be reviewed next. Read-only — does not modify anything.
tools.name: nexus_rehearsal_plan

tools.description: Run the memory rehearsal (sleep) cycle over the whole pool: rehearses every due memory (strengthens importance/confidence, reschedules the next review with a longer interval), schedules first rehearsals for fresh memories, and decays old never-rehearsed memories so they stop competing for context space. Returns a report of what was rehearsed, scheduled and decayed. Safe to run any time.
tools.name: nexus_rehearsal_cycle

tools.description: Mark a single memory as rehearsed right now — call this after a human (or the AI) actually reviewed the memory. Strengthens the memory slightly, bumps its rehearsal counter and reschedules the next review with a longer interval.
tools.name: nexus_rehearse_memory

tools.description: Preview how the Memory Firewall would treat a piece of incoming content before it is stored: returns a verdict (allow|block|quarantine), heuristic scores (toxicity, spam, prompt-injection, pii) and the reasons. Read-only — does not store anything. Use it to screen AI-generated or imported text before calling nexus_create_memory.
tools.name: nexus_firewall_check

tools.description: List all user-defined Memory Firewall rules: each rule has a pattern (matched case-insensitively in title+content), an action (block|quarantine), an enabled flag, an optional reason and its creation time.
tools.name: nexus_firewall_rules

tools.description: Add a user-defined Memory Firewall rule. When the pattern is found in incoming content, the rule overrides the heuristics: action 'block' rejects the content outright, action 'quarantine' parks it in the quarantine table for a human to approve or reject. Pattern matching is case-insensitive substring matching.
tools.name: nexus_firewall_rule_add

tools.description: Delete a user-defined Memory Firewall rule by id.
tools.name: nexus_firewall_rule_delete

tools.description: List quarantine entries — content the firewall screened but did not hard-block. Default shows pending entries that need a human decision. Pass status=pending|approved|rejected to filter, or status=all for everything.
tools.name: nexus_quarantine_list

tools.description: Approve a quarantined entry: creates a real memory from its content (bypassing the firewall — the human explicitly confirmed it) and marks the entry approved. The memory goes through the normal classification, conflict detection and semantic indexing pipelines.
tools.name: nexus_quarantine_approve

tools.description: Reject a quarantined entry: the content is permanently discarded (marked rejected) and never enters the memory store.
tools.name: nexus_quarantine_reject

tools.description: Manually log an operation into the flight recorder (the system's black box). Use it to record significant agent actions that are not automatically captured: category, action, summary, entity, outcome and optional details. Nothing is stored in memory — only appended to the operation journal.

action.description: Verb describing the operation, e.g. create_memory, resolve_conflict, run_cycle

category.description: memory | conflict | firewall | rehearsal | radar | skill | context | team | versioning | mcp | system

duration_ms.description: Optional duration of the operation in ms

tools.name: nexus_flight_log

tools.description: List the most recent flight recorder entries (the system's operation black box). Optionally filter by category. Useful to understand what the system has been doing and why.

category.description: Filter: memory | conflict | firewall | rehearsal | radar | skill | context | team | versioning | mcp | system

tools.name: nexus_flight_recent

tools.description: Replay the full operation chain of one entity from the flight recorder — every recorded step that touched the entity, chronological. Like reading the black box of a specific memory: created, quarantined, approved, updated, superseded, etc.
tools.name: nexus_flight_replay

tools.description: List currently active flight recorder sessions — what operation runs are in progress right now (agent passes, tool batches, tasks).
tools.name: nexus_flight_active_sessions

tools.description: Flight recorder summary statistics: total records, sessions, active sessions, and counts broken down by category and outcome. A health check for the operation black box.
tools.name: nexus_flight_stats

tools.description: Explain a past AI answer: fetch a recorded context chain by id and return 'Why did AI say this?' — a breakdown of which memory seeds and pipeline stages produced the answer, with an ASCII bar chart of context shares by category and the most influential memories. Call it whenever a user asks why a previous answer came out the way it did.
tools.name: nexus_why

tools.description: Record the full context chain of an answer: the query, intent, answer confidence, memory seeds used (kind, memoryId, title, weight, tokens) and pipeline stages (stage, durationMs, note). Every model answer becomes explainable afterwards via nexus_why.

query.description: The user query that started the pipeline

seeds_json.description: JSON array of {kind, memoryId, title, weight, tokens}

tools.name: nexus_context_chain_record

tools.description: List recently recorded context chains (newest first) with their query, intent, answer confidence and 'why' breakdown. Use it to find the id of a past answer you need to explain.
tools.name: nexus_context_chain_recent

tools.description: Get the identity passport of an agent: role, memory scope, trust level, available skills, allowed tools and constraints. Use it to confirm who you are and what you are allowed to do before acting. Falls back to the default primary passport when the name does not exist.
tools.name: nexus_passport_get

tools.description: List all agent identity passports registered in the system. Each passport describes an agent's role (generalist, coder, researcher, reviewer, orchestrator, memory-keeper), memory scope, trust level and allowed skills/tools/constraints.
tools.name: nexus_passport_list

tools.description: Create or update an agent identity passport by name. Fields update in place when the passport exists, or create a fresh one. Role is one of generalist, coder, researcher, reviewer, orchestrator, memory-keeper; memory_scope is personal, project, team or global; trust_level is 1..10 (how much the agent's memories can be trusted).

constraints.description: Things the agent must NOT do

tools.description: Allowed MCP tool names

tools.name: nexus_passport_upsert

tools.description: Render an agent's passport as a compact markdown block (identity, role, skills, tools, constraints, trust). Use it to attach the passport to a context package or an AGENTS.md file so the AI knows its own boundaries.
tools.name: nexus_passport_render

tools.description: Add a new member to the team roster. The team roster powers the trusted decision layer (who confirmed what, what went stale, what is in conflict). Role is one of admin, member, viewer (default member).
tools.name: nexus_team_add_member

tools.description: List all members of the team roster with their roles and active flags.
tools.name: nexus_team_list_members

tools.description: Update a team member's role and/or active flag by id.
tools.name: nexus_team_update_member

tools.description: Remove a team member from the roster by id.
tools.name: nexus_team_remove_member

tools.description: The trusted decision layer of the team: who confirmed which decision, what went stale (superseded), what is in conflict, and per-member activity (authored/confirmed/updated counts). This is the answer to 'what does the team actually know and agree on' — teams cannot get this from chat history.
tools.name: nexus_team_overview

tools.description: Reconstruct the full decision chain for one memory — the answer to 'why did we decide this?'. Returns the decision context (reason), the alternatives that were considered and rejected, who confirmed the decision and when, which memory it superseded and which replaced it, and the full version history (who changed what, with diff reasons). Use this for compliance questions like 'why did we choose PostgreSQL in March?' — prove the team knew and why it decided so.

memoryId.description: Memory id to reconstruct the audit trail for

tools.name: nexus_audit_trail

tools.description: Append a raw event to a memory's decision journal: Created, Confirmed, Superseded or Note. Every auditable action on a memory gets one row so the full chain 'why did we decide this' can be reconstructed. actor is who performed the action (member / user / system). For Superseded events pass relatedMemoryId pointing at the memory that replaced it.

memoryId.description: Memory id the event belongs to

relatedMemoryId.description: For Superseded: the memory that replaced this one

tools.name: nexus_audit_add_event

tools.description: Record that an alternative was considered for a decision (and rejected). Appends an Alternative event with { title, reason } to the memory's decision journal, so the compliance chain shows which options were weighed and why they lost.

memoryId.description: Memory id the decision belongs to

reason.description: Why it was not chosen (e.g. license costs)

title.description: The alternative that was considered (e.g. MySQL)

tools.name: nexus_audit_alternative

tools.description: List the six cognitive layers (Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Decision, Strategic) with their meaning and what promotes to them. Use this before classifying anything — the layer ladder answers 'what kind of knowledge is this?'.
tools.name: nexus_layers_list

tools.description: Distribution of memories across cognitive layers with mean classifier confidence per layer. Reveals the shape of the knowledge pool — where the project has facts vs decisions vs principles. Use it to answer 'what does the project actually know?'.
tools.name: nexus_layer_stats

tools.description: Explicitly assign a cognitive layer to a memory (user override). Records full provenance: confidence 1.0, reason, and a history entry tagged 'user' that pins the layer against auto-reclassification. Layer names: Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Decision, Strategic.

layer.description: One of: Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Decision, Strategic

reason.description: Why this layer (optional, recorded in history)

tools.name: nexus_layer_set

tools.description: Re-run the signature classifier on a memory and persist the result (with a history entry tagged 'classifier'). No-op if the layer is user-pinned. Use when content changed and the layer may be stale.
tools.name: nexus_layer_reclassify

tools.description: Full provenance trail of a memory's layer: every assignment (layer, confidence, reason, timestamp, by=user|classifier|migration), newest first. Answers 'why is this memory on this layer?'.
tools.name: nexus_layer_history

tools.description: List conflict groups — semantic contradictions between memories (both sides marked Conflicted). Optional status filter (open|resolved). Use this to find 'what does the project disagree with itself about?' and to surface open conflicts that need a decision.
tools.name: nexus_conflict_list

tools.description: One conflict group by id: topic, member memory ids, status, and the stored resolution (winner, confidence, reasons, by=user|engine, when). Use before resolving to see the full picture of the contradiction.
tools.name: nexus_conflict_details

tools.description: Run the Current Truth Engine over a conflict's members (read-only, nothing persisted). Returns the current winner, normalized confidence (0–1) and human-readable reasons ('+ recent source', '+ user confirmation'). Use to answer 'which memory is right RIGHT NOW?' before deciding anything.
tools.name: nexus_conflict_truth

tools.description: Settle a conflict: the winner becomes Current (engine) or UserConfirmed (user), every loser becomes Superseded (linked back to the winner), the group is marked resolved with full resolution provenance. When the engine's confidence is below 0.70 and a human must pick, this records the human verdict.

reason.description: Optional human reason for the resolution

winnerId.description: Memory id that wins the conflict

tools.name: nexus_conflict_resolve

tools.description: Full conflict health check: reconcile conflict groups with the current Conflicted records (clustering duplicates into existing open groups), then report every open conflict with the engine's current verdict. One call to know 'is the knowledge pool self-consistent, and if not, what exactly contradicts what?'.
tools.name: nexus_conflict_check

tools.description: Nexus Memory Score — health panel of the project's memory: coverage (share of graph entities covered by memories), freshness, consistency, trust, redundancy, conflict rate and context quality (maturity of knowledge across cognitive layers), plus an overall MEMORY HEALTH percentage. Use it to answer 'how healthy is this project's brain?' and to spot where memory needs attention (stale, redundant, conflicted).
tools.name: nexus_memory_score

tools.description: Context Lab — runs one query through multiple context-building strategies (compact / balanced / rich), measures each: memories included, tokens, maturity of cognitive layers, average relevance, build time, and a PREDICTED ACCURACY of the answer per strategy, then recommends the best one. Use it to answer 'how much context is enough for this question?' and to tune the engine's strategy per query type.

query.description: The question to build context for

tools.name: nexus_context_lab_run

tools.description: Context Lab history — returns recent lab experiments (newest first): which strategies won on which queries and the measured accuracy predictions. Use it to see what Nexus learned about choosing a context strategy.
tools.name: nexus_context_lab_history

tools.description: Context Lab stats — how many experiments were run and which strategy wins most often overall. Use it to check whether Nexus is converging on a preferred context strategy.
tools.name: nexus_context_lab_stats

tools.description: Skill Genesis — scans the flight log for REPEATED operations (same category+action performed N+ times) and proposes turning them into skills. Returns the new proposals with generated names, descriptions and occurrence counts. Use it to answer 'what are we doing over and over that should be a skill?' — Nexus noticing its own habits, no other project does this.

limit.description: How many recent flight records to analyze (default 2000)

minOccurrences.description: Minimum repetitions to become a candidate (default 3)

tools.name: nexus_skill_genesis_scan

tools.description: Skill Genesis — list the current skill candidates (status: proposed | approved | rejected | all). Use it to review what Nexus discovered as repeatable operations before approving or rejecting them.
tools.name: nexus_skill_genesis_candidates

tools.description: Skill Genesis — approve a candidate: creates a real runnable skill in the skills table (name + generated description; command placeholder, to be filled by the agent) and marks the proposal approved. Pass the proposal id from nexus_skill_genesis_candidates.
tools.name: nexus_skill_genesis_approve

tools.description: Skill Genesis — reject a candidate: marks it rejected (no skill is created) so it is not proposed again. Pass the proposal id.
tools.name: nexus_skill_genesis_reject

tools.description: Predictive Context — predicts the NEXT question the user is likely to ask, based on the Markov chain of past queries (every build_context call is remembered automatically). Returns ranked predictions with confidence, the predicted intent and the entities to prewarm in the context cache. Use it to answer 'what will they ask next?' and to pre-load context so the next answer comes instantly — no other project anticipates the user's next question like this.

query.description: The current question, to predict what comes next

tools.name: nexus_predictive_predict

tools.description: Predictive Context stats — how many queries are in the history (the larger the history, the smarter the next-question predictions).
tools.name: nexus_predictive_stats

tools.description: Knowledge Navigation 2.0 — renders the AI Universe map for an entity: concentric rings (Mission / Relevant / Supporting / Historical) around a concept, built from graph neighbors, linked memories, open conflicts and superseded records. Returns an ASCII-art map that shows what is mission-critical, what supports it, and what has been superseded — navigate any project space like a star chart, nothing else does this.

entityId.description: Entity id to build the map around

tools.name: nexus_knowledge_map

tools.description: Memory Rehearsal — canonical consolidation: finds records that state the same fact and collapses them into one Canonical Memory (e.g. 7 notes about JWT auth become one 'Authentication uses JWT access tokens + rotating refresh tokens'), boosting importance/confidence by repetition while keeping full provenance (derived_from). Run it in the sleep cycle — this is how Nexus' memory evolves on its own.
tools.name: nexus_rehearsal_consolidate

tools.description: List the canonical memories produced by consolidation — the distilled truths of the project (one record instead of many duplicates). Pass limit (default 25).

limit.description: How many canonical memories to return (default 25)

tools.name: nexus_canonical_memories

tools.description: Firewall agent permissions — create/update the policy of WHO may see WHAT memory. Pass agent name, optional role, allowed visibility (public,private,restricted; comma-separated, empty=all), allowed layers (working,episodic,semantic,procedural,decision,strategic; empty=all), deny patterns (comma-separated; any match in title/summary/content denies the agent). Example: Claude Code sees architecture/code/decisions but never secrets or personal memory — enterprise-grade access control, not a plain ACL.
tools.name: nexus_agent_policy_add

tools.description: List all agent-level memory permission policies — who may see what memory categories, layers and visibilities, plus deny patterns.
tools.name: nexus_agent_policy_list

tools.description: Firewall access control — check whether a specific agent may see a specific memory (by memory id) BEFORE it is injected into the LLM context. Returns allow/deny with the reasons (visibility, layer or deny pattern) and the memory sensitivity level (public/project/restricted/private). Use this to enforce 'what should this agent know' — the second ring of the Memory Firewall.

memoryId.description: Memory id to check access for

tools.name: nexus_agent_access_check
